content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file in one pass, so I'm planning a rich dungeon prop cluster — barrels, crates, a brazier, treasure chest, skull pile, bookshelf — aiming for roughly 150-250 parts using the builder API to place each part with position and rotation.

For texturing I'll define pixel tile textures (wood planks, stone bricks, metal) and use tileBox/cellPaint helpers so parts render with their own painted colors rather than tinted white, building barrels with lathe geometry and a small flagstone floor patch to ground the scene, then start laying out individual props like the chest with its lid starting at the origin.

Still designing the chest lid and barrel geometry...

Now I'm layering in more dungeon props: a crate stack with one box rotated on top, a brazier made from a pole and lathe bowl with glowing flame boxes, and a skull pile using small textured boxes for faces. I'm also adding scattered bones as rods, plus a candle, book, potions, and keys to round out the scene.

I'm figuring out a helper function for placing tiled boxes with rotation and texture tinting, and planning the wood texture as a pixel-based plank pattern.

Still writing textures...

Now I'm sketching the barrel shape as a lathe profile with a bulging outline and defining its overall height.

Still calculating hoop positions...

For coins I'll scatter small gold cylinders across the chest and floor, maybe 25 instances. For the skull I'm designing an 8x8 pixel-art texture with white/black pixel rows to form eye sockets and teeth pattern.

Now I'm planning potion bottles as small lathe shapes with colored glass and optional glow, and a book made from simple colored boxes with a lighter page edge. I'm also considering adding a broken stone wall backdrop behind the scene, roughly 2 units wide and 0.9 tall, with a crumbled irregular top edge to add composition depth.

Laying out the brick wall as two rows of individually placed blocks across eight columns, varying heights for a weathered look, plus a hanging chain with shackles made from small rod shapes. I'm placing the wall near the back edge and sizing the floor as a grid of flagstone tiles with slight gaps between them for texture.

Now I'm adding a floor-standing brazier with three rod legs and a lathed bowl, then moving on to the treasure chest -- building the wooden body and iron reinforcing bands as layered box shapes.

Still working out chest lid geometry...

Now I'm adding the band scaling and a gold lock plate at the lid/body junction, then working out scene layout: placing the chest near the front with coins spilling onto the floor, and positioning a couple of barrels off to the side at varying distances.

I'm also checking crate placements for overlap against the back wall and adjusting barrel positions so their radii don't clip into the wall, nudging coordinates until everything fits cleanly.

Then I'm adding scene dressing: a brazier near the left, a skull pile with a candle on the right, and considering a broken pillar or chest, but deciding to skip it and instead stack books and potions on top of the first crate to fill the space.

Placing potion bottles on the small crate's top surface and a lit candle atop the second barrel. I'm also adding a hanging chain with a shackle ring on the wall, using a partial torus for the ring geometry to suggest rusted ironwork.

Skipping the banner and cobweb details, but letting the floor texture carry moss accents. Total scene height lands around 0.94, which works fine.

Now I'm setting up the build with a texel constant, random seed, a color ramp helper, and starting the wood tile generation function.

Writing wood grain pixels...

Now moving to the stone tile generation with brick rows and mortar lines.

I'm planning the floor tile size, choosing a 40x40 flag texture with borders, bevel highlights, speckles, moss, and cracks. Then I'll handle a dark 16x16 iron texture with rivets for bands and braziers, and a 24x24 crate texture with planked frame and X-brace.
